record_type_quote: Here we describe replication results from 22 independent schizophrenia case-control datasets from the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium (n = 39,830).

targets.authors: Keller MC, Simonson MA, Ripke S, Neale BM, Gejman P V., Howrigan DP, et al.
targets.title: Runs of homozygosity implicate autozygosity as a schizophrenia risk factor.
targets.outcome_quote: The current study was a well-powered, direct replication attempt that failed to replicate an earlier finding that autozygosity arising from distant common ancestors was significantly associated with schizophrenia.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The conclusion explicitly states that the direct replication failed. The pooled original plus replication result and verification of original analyses do not change the verdict on the independent replication.

reasoning: The independent case-control sample directly retests Keller et al. (2012). The earlier methodological Keller paper, other prior association studies, and prior replication attempts are background or methods rather than additional targets. Original-data reanalysis verifies the pipeline; independent new-sample replication is the central study.
